report:
Theorem 8 contains a false coercivity assertion in its supplied scope. Its final sentence requires U_μ<∞, or equivalently the finite target conditions established under M₀. The reference bound M₀ alone does not imply coercivity. This missing target hypothesis is a scope defect, rather than a harmless notation correction.

Here is an actual counterexample using only the supplied grants. Take a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field in the original characteristic/residue-characteristic-zero domain, X=P¹, L=O(1), V=1, and the standard Gauss reference ψ. Write ζ for its Gauss point and p for z=0. N gives MA(0)=δ_ζ and u(ζ)=sup u for every actual psh potential. Consequently M₀=0 for every normalized E¹ potential. Choose a with 0<|a|<1 and put ℓ_m=−m log|a|. The sections T₁ and a^mT₀ generate O(1) and define the continuous pure FS potential
u_m(z)=log max(|z|,exp(−ℓ_m))−log max(1,|z|).
It has sup u_m=u_m(ζ)=0. Q identifies its genuine curvature as δ_{y_m}, where y_m is the Gauss point of the disk D(0,|a|^m). Both u_m(p) and u_m(y_m) equal −ℓ_m. O's curve energy identity therefore gives E(u_m)=−ℓ_m/2. For the positive Radon target μ=δ_p, of the required raw mass one,
B(u_m)=ℓ_m/2→∞, while E(u_m)−∫u_m dμ=ℓ_m/2→+∞.
This contradicts the stated coercivity sentence despite M₀=0. Moreover, O's real convexity and affine curvature law give B(tu_m)=t²ℓ_m/2. Taking t=ℓ_m^(−1/2) for large m produces normalized unit-cost tests with A_μ(tu_m)=√ℓ_m→∞, so U_μ=∞. The displayed bounds in Theorem 8 remain valid as extended bounds; they yield coercivity only when U_μ is finite. The same qualification is needed in note n4. The counterexample does not depend on any unresolved external source check.

Lemma 1: the bounded nonnegative flat Čech argument is correct. Separatedness over an affine base makes finite affine intersections affine. Invertible sections on an intersection form a rank-one projective module over its flat chart ring, hence an R-flat module. With Z^q=ker(d^q) and Z^m=C^m, higher exactness gives the descending short exact sequences used in the proof. A flat quotient makes each sequence tensor-exact and its kernel flat, including the degree-zero kernel. Thus arbitrary modules and nonflat algebras preserve the asserted cohomology. Proper Noetherian coherent-cohomology finiteness supplies finite presentation of H⁰, and finitely presented flat modules are projective. The negative-degree example correctly demonstrates why an arbitrary perfect complex cannot replace this hypothesis.

Theorem 2: its internal argument preserves the explicit existing-pair scope. Restricted series reduce to polynomials modulo a^j; flatness and finite equations give flat finitely presented reductions. Rank one makes the maximal ideal modulo a^j nil without requiring a uniform nilpotence exponent. The cited thickening results have the required finite-type and Cartesian hypotheses. Positive component degrees give residual ampleness, followed by ampleness on the whole reduction. Finite scheme, inverse-bundle, evaluation and cocycle data descend; properness, flatness and ampleness can then be imposed at a common later stage because they persist under subsequent base change. Serre theory is applied at the Noetherian stage, followed by Lemma 1 for arbitrary base change. The a^j layers, whole-mod-a H¹ vanishing, compatible section lifting, inverse-limit equalizer and convergent division are sound. Integral coefficients and exact generation force max|f_i|=1 at every generic analytic point. Once the analytic sections are identified with algebraic sections, this also excludes algebraic common zeros and gives the denominator kd on the same original bundle. No carrier replacement or universal model existence follows.

Theorem 2's external certification remains incomplete independently of the counterexample. FK's stronger adhesive domain matches R, a and K=R[1/a]. Its printed comparison uses coherent lifts, formal comparison and localization. The recursive Raynaud–Gruson proof and rigid/Berkovich section comparison remain unchecked. The broader announced comparison does not discharge these checks. Immediate Stacks proof units were inspected, but their entire recursive Chow and flat-locus foundations were not reconstructed. Thus this report does not separately certify Theorem 2 under the task's full source-audit threshold.

Lemma 3: on the actual shrunken étale chart, every reduction of the zero fibre is étale and finitely presented. Arbitrary-thickening finiteness makes it finite étale; the single rational residue point gives rank one over the local base. The structural map, identified by evaluation, is an isomorphism. Monicity proves regularity on the polynomial base, and étale flatness preserves it. Compatible, unique quotients establish ker(ev)=(τ), closedness, B/(τ)=R and the original generic evaluation. Equal principal Cartier ideals have unit ratios. The signed horizontal degrees are correct for the stated actual rational sections and specified meromorphic divisor. Existence of adapted charts is not established by this implication.

Lemma 4: xy=π and base flatness establish the needed nonzerodivisors. The equations c_v and c_vx^k give unit overlap ratios because the scalar ratio has norm one. The canonical generic trivialization preserves the actual generic bundle. Integral units and their inverses have norm one at every analytic point, giving the stated metric. Residual branch orders are k and −k; both incidences of a loop must be counted. Their sum cancels. Rational slopes require clearing denominators. These calculations establish the implication on a supplied full cover, without constructing such covers universally.

Theorem 5: the weighted Laplacian has constant kernel and zero-sum image, including the two incidences of loops. Mixing with the uniform measure on every old vertex creates a strictly positive minimum margin. Shared Γ-heights close every cycle; rational brackets and the specified movable bends give exact endpoint equations, Γ-valued bend positions and heights, and positive new masses. Finite valence controls the old masses. Uniform errors tend to zero, and incidence cancellation preserves raw mass V. The numerical irrational-cycle example has the stated bends and masses. The one-vertex edgeless case is immediate and should be stated separately from the valence estimate. Any later vertex insertion requires restarting positivity.

Lemma 6: its stated canonical-reduction, single-Shilov and value-group hypotheses suffice. Single-Shilov norming proves the natural reduction embedding. A norm-one fraction can be normalized by one common scalar from C, and completion approximation with error below one preserves its residue. This proves the natural residual-field equality. A singleton reduction fibre alone supplies neither the norming assertion nor this equality.

The CLDv1 discussion correctly distinguishes atomic support from coefficients and keeps the universal application pending. The residual bundle, residual-field identification, calibrated coefficient calculation and algebraically closed factor-one case are separate obligations. The intended curve coefficients are deg(M|Y)/d, with no probability normalization, field-degree multiplier or factorial. The displayed formula is not used to identify an unrecognized graph measure with O's genuine operator. BPR and GH statements retain their actual-model domains. GM A.7 concerns subfields of the completed algebraic closure, and does not justify an arbitrary transcendental extension outside it. The exact BL85 scan could not be retrieved here; its historical visual-inspection claims were not independently validated. These supporting-route limitations are not antecedents of the genus-zero proof.

Theorem 7: the convex-series proof correctly applies extended energy before establishing nontriviality or E¹ membership. Compactness excludes an identically −∞ endpoint despite the absence of a common finite-valued anchor. Sequential monotone convergence then gives the contradiction. Positive scaling proves the converse. Finite continuous dual gives integrability and equality with the all-E¹ dual through the stated continuous/lsc Radon-net argument: directed open levels, compact inner approximation, finite subcovers and one common index. It does not use arbitrary measurable-net monotone convergence.

Theorem 8's Bernstein identity and constants are correct relative to O. The sum of A_k is (n+1)B, the positive-degree Bernstein terms are bounded by ns, and integration gives D_n=n(n+1)/2 for every real t∈[0,1]. Under M₀ and finite U_μ, the chosen positive t yields the asserted integral bound, J bound and coercivity. Continuous reference estimates extend by supremum convergence and the Radon-net law. The curve identity and raw V² factors are correct. The unqualified coercivity sentence is the concrete defect identified above.

Corollary 9 is correct for an already known genuine output: O supplies all-test integrability, concavity and the finite supporting derivative. Continuous majorants recover the finite maximizing value. It supplies no inverse existence or every-point uniqueness theorem.

Lemma 10: energy symmetry against Q's genuine continuous inverse atoms gives the stated kernel representation with the correct raw factor V. Retraction yields the finite-tree Laplacian. Kernel derivatives have bounded variation; Stieltjes integration with the Lipschitz positive part includes every vertex term and gives the negative Dirichlet integral. Positivity and vanishing on S force the maximum bound. Attached branches have nonnegative kernel increments, and continuity recovers terminal points. A singleton spanning tree is handled directly by the branch argument. Type-II/III atoms suffice for the finite-tree proof; terminal values follow by continuity.

Theorem 11: the supplied proof correctly establishes the new grant applications. Flat field Čech base change gives H¹(O)=0 and H⁰(O)=E. The degree-one point sequence provides an actual basepoint-free two-section system. Its finite degree-one map to the normal projective line is an isomorphism, with the actual rational bundle then identified using Q. Completion of the algebraic closure is algebraically closed: coefficient approximations to a monic polynomial admit successively close algebraic roots, bounded by the appropriate root of the coefficient error, and hence a convergent root. The transported Gauss metric has a finite actual Galois orbit. Q's uniqueness identifies repeated orbit atoms after normalization; only finite continuous metrics are averaged. Lemma 10 and invariance establish every downstairs FS maximum at the descended atom before N is applied. D's finite-dual lift and Q's actual split equation produce a normalized invariant singular solution before D descent. For every downstairs solution, O's pushforward and equivariance plus D's lift uniqueness identify its upstairs target; Q and quotient surjectivity then give every-point equality modulo one finite constant. T handles precisely the trivial boundary. This genus-zero argument uses the finite target conditions and is unaffected by the false unrestricted coercivity assertion.

Harmless clarifications are: read affine invertible modules as rank-one projective modules; use Z^q=ker(d^q) explicitly in Lemma 1; handle the edgeless graph separately; replace the stray pi_e notation by π_e; and retain zero-coefficient omission at poles and both loop incidences. Adding finite U_μ to the coercivity assertion changes its stated quantified scope and is not included among these harmless corrections.

Only the six supplied whole grants and unchanged clarifications were treated as grants. Registered notes, hashes, builds, finite grids and historical review status were not mathematical acceptance. Premises 14 and 15 lack verified original-primary quotation bindings because retrieval did not yield their pertinent proof units; no quotation has been invented for them. The original arbitrary-dimensional P16.4, universal positive-genus realization and general prescribed-target existence remain open.

premises: If A is Noetherian, X→Spec(A) is proper and F is coherent, then H^i(X,F) is a finite A-module for every i≥0 (Stacks 30.19.2, Tag 02O6).

For a Cartesian morphism of arbitrary thickenings (X⊂X')→(Y⊂Y'), with both induced morphisms locally of finite type, finiteness and properness of the induced morphisms are equivalent (Stacks 37.3.4(2),(8), Tag 0BPG).
Relative ampleness of an invertible sheaf is invariant under arbitrary thickenings of the source and base (Stacks 37.3.2, Tag 0D2R).

For a proper scheme X of dimension at most one over a field, an invertible sheaf is ample if and only if its degree is positive on every one-dimensional irreducible component (Stacks 33.44.15, Tag 0B5Y).

For a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition maps, finitely presented schemes over the limit descend to a stage; morphisms descend to a later stage, and equal morphisms become equal at a later stage (Stacks 32.10.1, Tag 01ZM).

Over a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions, finitely presented quasi-coherent sheaves and their morphisms descend, equalities hold at a later stage, and invertible sheaves descend as invertible sheaves (Stacks 32.10.2–3, Tags 01ZR and 0B8W).

Let S=lim S_i with S_i quasi-compact quasi-separated and transition maps affine. For a morphism f_0:X_0→Y_0 between finitely presented S_0-schemes, if f_0 is locally of finite type and its base change to S is proper, then its base change to some S_i is proper (Stacks 32.13.1, Tag 081F).

Let S=lim S_i with S_i quasi-compact quasi-separated and transition maps affine. For a locally finitely presented morphism f_0:X_0→Y_0 between finitely presented S_0-schemes, flatness after base change to S implies flatness after base change to some S_i (Stacks 32.8.7, Tag 04AI).

For a Cartesian directed system (R_λ→S_λ,M_λ) of finitely presented algebras and finitely presented modules, whose colimit module M is flat over the colimit ring R, the modules M_λ are flat over R_λ for all sufficiently large λ (Stacks 10.168.1(3), Tag 02JO).

For a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions, an invertible sheaf on an initial stage whose pullback to the limit is ample has ample pullback at some later stage (Stacks 32.4.15, Tag 09MT).

If R is Noetherian, X→Spec(R) is proper, L is ample invertible and F is coherent, then all H^i(X,F) are finite, sufficiently high twists F⊗L^k are generated by finitely many global sections, and H^i(X,F⊗L^k)=0 for every i>0 and all sufficiently large k (Stacks 30.16.1 and 30.14.1, Tags 0B5T and 01YS).

Every a-adically complete valuation ring V, with a∈m_V\{0}, and every topologically finitely generated V-algebra are topologically universally adhesive (Fujiwara–Kato 1308.4734v5, 0.9.2.7 and I.2.1.4(2)).

Over a complete topologically universally adhesive adic ring A of finite ideal type, coherent higher direct images for proper morphisms of separated finite-type schemes over U=Spec(A)\V(I) commute with rigid analytification (Fujiwara–Kato 1308.4734v5, II.9.4.1–2).

Let B be universally coherent, I finitely generated, (B,I) universally adhesive, X/B proper finitely presented and F coherent. For every q≥0, completed H^q(X,F) is canonically isomorphic to H^q(X̂,F̂) and to lim_j H^q(X,F/I^(j+1)F) (Fujiwara–Kato 1308.4734v5, I.9.1.3–9.2.1).

If X→S is locally finitely presented and the weakly associated points of O_S form a locally finite set, then the S-flat locus of any finite-type O_X-module M is open and M is finitely presented on that locus (Raynaud–Gruson, Critères de platitude et de projectivité, Première partie 3.4.6, https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01390094).

For a projective scheme over a complete nontrivially valued rank-one field and a coherent algebraic sheaf, its rigid and Berkovich analytifications have canonically identical global sections, compatibly with algebraic analytification and strict-affinoid restriction (Berkovich, Étale cohomology for non-Archimedean analytic spaces, §1.6, https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1993__78__5_0.pdf).
